NBE Values
The National Bank of Egypt (NBE) was established on the 25th of June 1898, as an Egyptian joint stock company, with a capital of GBP 1 mn. It was the first bank to issue banknotes in Egypt, as it assumed the functions of the central bank until 1960. As of January 1, 1961, NBE continued to act purely as a commercial bank, becoming the oldest commercial bank in Egypt. Since its establishment, the Bank has been the cornerstone of Egypt’s national economy, thanks to its effective contributions to financing mega national projects.
NBE has always been committed to supporting the path of development. It has enriched the economic scene through expanding its banking activities and services and reaching out to citizens. The Bank holds the largest customer base in the Egyptian banking sector. In December 2024, NBE commanded a market share of 36.8% in terms of deposits and 47.5% in terms of loans. The Bank also maintains the widest network of branches with 679 branches, offices, and units, along with 7,232 automatic teller machines (ATMs) spread across the country, in addition to 633,000 point of sale (POS) machines. This emphasizes the Bank’s continuous commitment to enabling all segments of society to access financial products and services that meet their diverse needs, affirming its dedication to being “The People’s Bank.”
NBE is always keen to deliver the latest, cutting-edge banking services and products to its customers to retain their valuable trust in the Bank and to maintain its leadership in the banking market, targeting a more advanced banking system and a more secure and sustainable future. In this regard, NBE has implemented an ambitious digital transformation plan, which includes the expansion of banking services through electronic channels and smart applications, such as Al Ahly Net and NBE PhoneCash, and launching a new generation of bus branches that offer banking services through alternative delivery channels. In addition, state-of-the-art cybersecurity systems are deployed to protect customer data in line with the highest global standards.
NBE’s presence extends beyond the local market, broadening its reach globally. The Bank maintains a strong international presence in most continents of the world through subsidiaries in the United Kingdom (UK) and Sudan (NBE-Juba in South Sudan); NBE’s branches in New York (United States of America) and Shanghai (China); and representative offices in Johannesburg (South Africa), Dubai (UAE), and Addis Ababa (Ethiopia), in addition to NBE (DIFC) Limited for Financial Advice in Dubai, UAE. In a momentous achievement, NBE announced the opening of its first branch in the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia (KSA) in October 2025, becoming the first Egyptian bank to have a branch in the Kingdom. This is in addition to a vast correspondent bank network around the globe (Europe – USA – Australia – Canada – the Far East – Africa – the Arabian Gulf).
The Bank offers top-tier funds transfer services to ensure that NBE is the domestic market leader in terms of receiving remittances from Egyptian expatriates. The Bank's management relies on its vast market experience and solid network of banking relationships with a large number of local, regional and international partners, including funds transfer companies, FinTech companies, and regional and local institutions.
During the year ending on December 31, 2024, NBE managed to achieve unprecedented, record-setting operating results. The Bank’s total financial position as at December 2024 recorded EGP 8.14 trillion, growing 55.5%. Total deposits reached EGP 4.96 trillion as at December 2024, with a growth rate of 32.9%, which highlights customers’ trust in NBE’s services and status. The total portfolio of loans and advances to customers and banks surged to EGP 3.95 trillion as at December 2024, growing 65%. Consequently, the Bank posted a profit (before taxes) of EGP 223.2 bn. and a profit (after taxes) of EGP 133.3 bn., with a growth rate of 88.5%.
NBE has maintained its preeminent role within the Egyptian banking sector through adopting advanced and dynamic strategies that align with both local and global developments. These strategies also ensure the Bank’s continued success in achieving its ambitious targets and plans and sustaining its leadership in the banking market. NBE has continued its leading role in driving transformation within the banking sector. This is achieved through its comprehensive (2025–2027) strategy, which embodies its commitment to development and innovation, based on key pillars that include digital transformation, artificial intelligence (AI) enablement, financial inclusion, strengthening the national role, sustainability, and sustainable finance".
Crowning its ongoing efforts and leadership at the banking sector level, NBE received numerous prestigious awards, including the “Best Bank for SMEs” in Egypt 2025 as part of the Euromoney Awards for Excellence. It is a global award given annually to celebrate leading financial institutions in the fields of bank performance, innovation, and customer service.
In addition, NBE was ranked first in Egypt and Africa by Bloomberg for undertaking the roles of administrative agent, mandated lead arranger, and book-runner of syndicated loans up until Q3 of 2025. It also ranked first as a documentation bank, fourth as an administrative agent and mandated lead arranger, and fifth as a book-runner in the Middle East and North Africa (MENA) region up until the same quarter. The Bank managed 25 finance deals, of which 20 — the largest number of deals to be managed in Africa — were managed by the Bank as an administrative agent, with a total amount of EGP 402 bn.
For the fourth year in a row, NBE managed to maintain the ISO 9001:2015 certification — obtained from the British Standards Institution (BSI) accredited by the United Kingdom Accreditation Service (UKAS) — for the quality management system of the Legal Group for 2025, becoming the first bank in Egypt, Africa, and the Middle East to receive the certification.
Moreover, NBE renewed the ISO 27001 certification for information security management system (ISMS) and ISO 27701 certification for privacy information management system (PIMS) for a new cycle (2025–2028). This, in turn, boosts customers’ confidence in the Bank’s digital services, reflects the Bank’s commitment to continuous improvement in information security metrics, and emphasizes the sound management and protection of customers’ personal information and the adoption of the highest standards of responsibility and transparency.

What is a current account?
Current accounts are demand deposits that provide accessible and unconditional cash deposit/ withdrawal into/from the account at any time.
Who are the persons entitled to open a current account?
Natural and legal persons.
What is the minimum amount for opening the account?
Minimum limit for account opening in local currency: EGP 2500 (individual) and EGP 5,000 (corporate)
Is it necessary to submit a proof of income source upon opening a current account?

Is it allowed to order a cheque book linked to the current account?
Yes, you may order a cheque book linked to the account as per the applicable procedures.
Is the account qualified to receive remittances?
You may receive remittances on the account via the account number and the SWIFT code of the branch holding the account.

National Bank of Egypt corporate governance framework
The National Bank of Egypt is committed to create value for its customers whilst meeting its statutory and regulatory obligations. Fundamental to the Board’s strategy are high standards of corporate governance, in particular, those laid down in the corporate governance regulations issued by Central Bank of Egypt . Our core values and standards, governance management frameworks, and internal controls work together to prevent, detect and respond to potential or actual fraudulent or corrupt conduct. NBE strive the best practice in corporate governance across our footprint. We believe that simply complying with written corporate governance standards is not enough , Its vital to have an underlying culture with behaviors and values that support corporate governance. It is the responsibility of all of our employees to be responsive and vigilant to ensure compliance with both the letter and the spirit of our governance framework. Therefore, We take care to ensure that all our employees have and demonstrate the necessary skills, values and experience commensurate with their responsibilities. We place as much emphasis on the way employees behave as on what they deliver.

How do I apply for credit cards?
Please complete the National Bank of Egypt credit card application form and submit it at your nearest NBE branch.
How do I collect my credit card after issuance?
Your credit card will be sent to you via a courier or the branch. You can check the progress of the application by contacting our customer service.
How do I activate my credit card?
You can activate your credit card through NBE ATMs/ Al Ahly Net / NBE Mobile or NBE call center 19623.
What is the minimum payment for the credit card?
The minimum payment is 5% of the outstanding balance.
Are there any interest rates charged in case of repaying the minimum payment?
Yes, an interest rate is calculated in case of repaying the minimum payment.
How do I pay my credit card?
There are several methods to pay your credit card (via the nearest branch, ATMs, Fawry outlets, and the transfer of funds from the cardholder's account via Al Ahly Net service).
Can I set up installment payments directly with the merchant?
Yes, you can set up installment payments with NBE accredited merchants for terms starting from 6 months and up to 36 months.
Can I set up installment payments for purchases from a non-NBE accredited merchant?
Purchases can be repaid in installments within the current month after contacting the customer service to apply for the installment by phone service.
Can any cash advance transaction be repaid in installments?
You can repay the amount of cash advance after contacting the customer service to apply for the installment by phone service.
How do I know the amounts payable on my card?
You can contact the customer service, use Al Ahly Net Service, review the paper statement of account sent to you monthly or inquire via ATMs.
What do I do if I do not receive my statement?
If you do not receive your statement, please contact our customer service to verify your address and the necessary action will be taken.
What if my card is lost?
You can contact our call center on 19623 to suspend the card and request a replacement.
Can the PIN code be changed?
Yes, the PIN code can be changed via ATMs after contacting the customer service.

NBE’s 1st Environmental Footprint Report
(FY June 2020 - December 2021)
The Environment (E) Pillar is not new to NBE with over 20 years of focus on pollution abatement and supporting the enforcement of environmental compliance through various lending programs, NBE played a key strategic role in supporting the government’s environmental agenda.
Our 1st Environmental Footprint Report is one of the most comprehensive reports, covering the broadest boundary spectrum and bank-wide internal operational premises, including head quarters, branches, training centers, and sports clubs. Fiscal year 2021 is considered our baseline year through which we shall start taking new measurements for decarbonisation and accelerating the transition to a low carbon and green economy.
NBE’s ENVIRONMENTAL FOOTPRINT (5 Footprints)
Carbon Footprint
The amount of Carbon Dioxide that an individual, group, or organization lets into the atmosphere in a certain time frame.
Applied Standards and Guidelines
The Greenhouse Gas Protocol Guidelines which include, but not limited to: A Corporate Accounting and Reporting Standard Corporate Value Chain (Scope 3) Accounting and Reporting Standard
ISO 14064-1: 2019, specification with guidance at the organization level for quantification and reporting of greenhouse gas emissions and removals
2006 Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC) Guidelines for Greenhouse Gas Inventories (with 2019 Refinements)
Results Summary
Water Footprint
Quantification of amount of water use throughout the business, measured in m3. Assessing the business’ activities within the set boundaries to find out where and for what purpose the water is used.
The water footprint network
Waste Footprint
The waste footprint falls under the Ecological Footprint as it measures how much we generate waste. Calculating the waste footprint enabled NBE to estimate the waste quantities that was generated as a result of the operations occurring at the organization.
British Standard for Waste management in buildings (BS 5906:2005)
Plastic Footprint
Quantification of plastic use within the business’ operations, measured in kilograms (kg). The same activities that have been covered in the Carbon Footprint are assessed.
Plastic Leak Project, Methodological Guidelines, and Quantis and EA. 2020 v1.1
VERRA Plastic Standard
Land Footprint
Quantification of the land area that is used to provide the needed resources to carry through the business activities. It is expressed as land area in global hectares, enabling businesses to operate within the natural biocapacity of the earth, and thus, not exploiting more than can be regenerated.
The global footprint network

This helps create a favorable business climate for Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) and entrepreneurs and expand digital financial services. The goal is to provide various financial products to all segments of society through the Bank’s official channels, with a focus on quality and cost-effectiveness while protecting the rights of the consumers of these services, enabling them to manage their finances effectively.

Financial inclusion accounts for retail customers (Al Mostakabal Savings Account), which can be opened without a minimum amount from the age of 16, with special interest rates.

NBE's Social Development
The National Bank of Egypt (NBE) supports social development efforts through an integrated strategy aimed at achieving sustainable development and improving the quality of life for citizens across all Egyptian governorates. The Bank places particular focus on the neediest areas to make a tangible impact on Egyptian citizens’ lives.
Furthermore, the Bank relies on continuous cooperation and coordination with government entities and civil society organizations to consolidate efforts, maximize the impact of initiatives, and ensure that services reach the widest possible segment of beneficiaries. This contributes to pushing forward the State’s development plans and realizing the objectives of Egypt Vision 2030.
Healthcare
NBE continues to strengthen the healthcare system by developing the healthcare infrastructure, equipping and operating hospitals and medical units, and supporting treatment initiatives and medical convoys that aim at providing healthcare services, eliminating patient waiting lists, and delivering appropriate treatment to the underprivileged individuals without imposing financial burdens, particularly in remote areas and the neediest villages, as access to healthcare is an intrinsic right of every Egyptian.
Education and vocational training
The Bank exerts sustained efforts to support and advance the educational process by developing schools and educational institutions, improving the learning environment, and granting scholarships as well as training and qualification programs for students at various educational levels. This contributes to developing young people's skills and preparing them for the labor market. In addition, the Bank places great importance on supporting students in Upper Egypt and the most vulnerable families by providing school supplies and helping alleviate the economic burden on such families. This enhances educational continuity and promotes the principle of equal opportunity among all segments of society, as supporting education is, really, the hope of future generations.
Urban and human development
NBE supports various initiatives and programs to empower women and youth, solidify economic and social development, and help families, so as to optimize their quality of life, achieve integrated development, and create a sustainable social impact. The Bank also supports the development of the neediest areas by funding family housing construction and development projects, particularly in Upper Egypt. Such projects aim to provide adequate housing for underprivileged families through arranging a living environment that enables families to settle down and improve their social and economic conditions.
Furthermore, NBE works on supporting and integrating people with disabilities through carrying out many initiatives to enhance their quality of life and strengthen their ability to be effectively part of the society and become impactful and productive members. The Bank believes in the importance of empowering all society groups to equally participate in the development process as comprehensive empowerment guarantees the advancement of society.
Environment and heritage
NBE supports environmental initiatives to protect the natural resources and preserve the environment. The Bank contributes to projects that address the effects of climate change, preserve the marine environment and promote environmental awareness and volunteering. In addition, the Bank is committed to supporting sustainable environmental solutions and promoting environmental awareness in the community besides preserving the cultural and heritage identity, keeping in mind that a protected environment guarantees a secured future.

Program introduction
What is GEFF?
GEFF offers technical support and consultancy free of charge to review and finance investment and operating costs for green economy projects.
What does GEFF offer?
Finance: Financing investment costs and running costs of targeted projects according to the following:
Financing investment costs of enterprises operating in all economic business activities.
Financing working capital only for enterprises or vendors that manufacture/provide energy efficient products.
Consultancy: Technical consultancy to evaluate investment feasibility and the economic/environmental return.
Eligible applicants
The program allows finance for enterprises that operate in all economic fields and offer the following products and services:
Renewable energy projects.
Efficient energy use.
Efficient energy management in buildings.
Water and waste water rationalization and reuse.
Sustainable land management.
Efficient use of natural resources and operation input of raw materials.
United Nations Industrial Development
Organization (UNIDO) Project Solar Heat for Industrial Processes (SHIP)
What is UNIDO?
UNIDO is a specialized agency of the United Nations (UN), primarily aiming to promote and accelerate industrial development in the developing countries and countries with economies in transition, and enhance international industrial cooperation.
What is SHIP?
SHIP is a program aimed at financing the investment costs of solar heating applications used in industrial projects.
Who is the beneficiary?
The program aims to finance small and medium industrial enterprises or medium and large corporates owned by the private sector, especially those operating in food processing, chemical manufacturing, and spinning and weaving.
What are the benefits?
The beneficiary will obtain an EGP facility for the project, in accordance with the following:
Technical and feasibility studies will be conducted by the project consultant free of charge.
Finance shall be up to 90% of the project's investment costs, provided that the customer's own contribution shall not be less than 10%.
Facility amount shall be determined based on the studies to be conducted by the project consultant.

National Bank of Egypt - Mentoring
About the EBRD Mentoring Network
The National Bank of Egypt is joining forces with EBRD to boost availability of digital mentoring services to the local business community, recognising the value added of tailored mentoring and support to small businesses in addition to accessing finance.
Part of the EBRD’s unique Youth in Business programme, we are helping provide young entrepreneurs with access to the finance, skills and networks they need to take their businesses further—and play the role in the economy that they deserve.
This initiative is financed by the EBRD in partnership with MicroMentor and the Mastercard Center for Inclusive Growth to increase access to mentoring services across North Africa and the Middle East.
About MicroMentor
A global community of mentors and entrepreneurs.
A program of Mercy Corps, MicroMentor's online business mentoring program enables the world's largest community of purpose-driven entrepreneurs and business mentors to create powerful connections, solve problems, and build successful businesses together.
Since 2008, MicroMentor has bridged geographical and cultural barriers between Entrepreneurs and Mentors, fostering more than 75,000 connections that span the globe.
https://www.micromentor.org/nbe/
MicroMentor FAQs:
Are there any mentoring fees?
Micro Mentor is a free of charge online platform aiming to help entrepreneurs. Members are able to ‘flag’ any entrepreneurs or mentors who ask for compensation for Micro Mentor’s 24/7 user support to respond to appropriately.
How can I find the right mentor to guide me through my career?
You can start by setting up a profile. You are 10 times more likely to connect with a mentor when your profile has a professional photo and complete descriptions. Mentors use this information to understand your business needs and motivations. Once your profile is complete, search for mentors who have the experience you’re looking for.
Can I write to a potential mentor in my local language?
The Micro Mentor platform experience is available in English, Arabic, Spanish, Bahasa Indonesia, and Somali, but mentors on the platform speak 20+ languages . You can use the search filters in the mentor search to narrow down the list of mentors to those who speak your language.
What’s in it for me?
Volunteering your skills with MicroMentor is a chance to become known as an experienced mentor in the MicroMentor community. Working as a mentor also helps to develop a better understanding of business challenges and build your communication, leadership, and management competencies.
How do I find the right entrepreneur to mentor?
You can start by setting up a profile on our online platform at
Make sure your profile is as complete as possible. Entrepreneurs can reach out to you while doing their own research looking for mentors, but you are also encouraged to search the entrepreneur profiles and reach out to those you’d like to help.
What if I don’t get a response?
If a user doesn’t respond to your message, try messaging several others until you find a few who are interested. Entrepreneurs are very busy - be patient and give them time to respond.
What is the time commitment?
Since every mentoring relationship is different, the time commitment and terms are largely up to you to decide with the entrepreneur. The average mentoring relationships lasts 12 hours over the course of 3 months.
This initiative is financed by @EBRDHQ in partnership with #Micro Mentor and Master card Center for Inclusive Growth to increase access to mentoring services across North Africa and the Middle East.

National Bank of Egypt - Exhibitions
Exhibitions
Agri Expo
January 20 to 22, 2025
The National Bank of Egypt (NBE) exclusively sponsored the 10th International Exhibition and Conference for Agricultural Supplies, “Agri Expo”, at the Green Desert Hotel, El-Maadawy (located at Km 84, Cairo-Alexandria Desert Road). Agri Expo features the largest companies in the agricultural sector, with specializations that span all its activities, including agricultural mechanization, agricultural supplies and materials, agricultural crops, modern irrigation systems, and renewable energy and environmental protection systems.
A number of discussion sessions were held to address NBE’s support for the agricultural sector, and several financing opportunities and consultancy services were offered to all Agri Expo visitors.
The Largest Industrial Event in Africa and the Middle East:
MacTech Exhibition
December 18 to 21, 2025
For the seventh year in a row, the 25th edition of MacTech Exhibition kicked off its events under NBE’s exclusive sponsorship. MacTech is considered the largest industrial event in Africa and the Middle East that serves the industrial sector, particularly engineering industries.
The exhibition featured three major industrial exhibitions serving all aspects of the industrial sector in the Egyptian market, namely:
MacTech exhibition for metal working, CNC machinery, and welding and cutting equipment.
Handling Expo for handling, storage and transmission equipment, cranes, and hoists.
Airtech Exhibition for compressed air technology and accessories.
NBE took part in the exhibition through holding a series of educational seminars on the Bank’s support for small and medium enterprises (SMEs) in the industrial sector.
HACE-Hotel Expo
October 7 to 9, 2025
NBE was the exclusive sponsor of the 45th edition of the international HACE-Hotel Expo 2025, which was held at the Cairo International Conference Centre (CICC) in Nasr City. The expo is Egypt’s largest international trade fair specializing in furnishings, supplies, and equipment that serve the hospitality sector, including restaurants, coffee shops, bakeries, and supermarkets. NBE contributed to supporting a large number of service business owners through its Al Ahly Business tailored programs.
Women Rise Bazaar
February 19 to 21, 2025
NBE organized the Women Rise Bazaar to support women entrepreneurs in the field of handicrafts.
In addition, NBE held training workshops for women entrepreneurs, provided mentorship and consultancy, and offered money collection solutions and financial inclusion accounts to help them develop their products, efficiently manage their businesses, and confidently prepare for the Bazaar.

National Bank of Egypt - BDS Hubs
Business Development Hubs
The Business Development Hubs of the National Bank of Egypt are dedicated to offering a range of non-financial services aimed at fostering innovation and entrepreneurship. These services are designed to assist in transforming creative ideas into viable projects, empowering aspiring young entrepreneurs, and creating a supportive ecosystem for the growth of small, medium, and startup enterprises across diverse economic sectors.
Services:
NBE's Business Development Services (BDS) hubs offer many services, including:
Training and capacity-building:
Validating your business idea:
This service assists customers and entrepreneurs in evaluating and identifying the applicable business ideas that suit their capabilities and experiences.
Starting your business and conducting feasibility studies :
The BDS hubs help customers and entrepreneurs develop and implement preliminary business plans or basic feasibility studies to start a new business or amend an existing one in order to identify the funding needs required to complete a project.
Business registration and licensing procedures:
The BDS hubs assist customers in accessing information on the locations, procedures, and documents required to officially register and/or obtain a license for a business. The BDS hubs also guide customers to the nearest one-stop-shop either in chambers of commerce, the Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises Development Agency (MSMEDA) or GAFI (General Authority for Investment).
Facilitating access to Finance
The BDS hubs:
Provide information and data to customers on financing products offered by banks or non-bank financial institutions (factoring companies, financial leasing companies, venture capital companies) according to the geographic location, business nature, and funding required.
Help customers prepare credit proposals and the documents required to consider the funding need.
Educate customers on how to deal with funding institutions, the sound administration of bank accounts, and factors that must be taken into account to avoid a poor credit rating at finance institutions.
Providing financial analysis and assessment:
The BDS hubs provide a preliminary and guiding financial analysis of the enterprise's financial statements and present its findings, financial ratios, and recommendations. They additionally prepare customers to make future or corrective decisions.
Networking with vendors and targeted markets:
Networking with vendors and targeted markets is a service provided in order to give the small and medium enterprises a hand to improve their products and services by:
Linking small and medium enterprises with commercial chains (public or private sectors).
Linking small and medium enterprises with enterprises of the same size to exchange products and services.
Sharing Knowledge and Information on SMEs:
This service is provided through business development specialists, offering specialized information and data that support entrepreneurs and SME owners at various stages of their business.
The service also includes linking customers to a diverse network of advisory service providers, in addition to providing information about entities and institutions that support entrepreneurs, such as:
Consulting firms (financial, economic, administrative, and marketing services)
Specialized advisory service providers
Business and product development experts
Institutions that support entrepreneurs and SMEs
Business incubators and accelerators
BDS hubs offer specialized training workshops delivered by business development specialists, in collaboration with specialized entities and institutions. Such workshops aim to develop the skills and capabilities of SME owners and it's employees, enabling them to manage their businesses efficiently and enhance their capacity for growth and sustainability.
Training programs include:
Developing administrative and operational skills
Enhancing technical expertise
Supporting planning and scaling capabilities
The programs also include entrepreneurial training programs that cover:
Identifying personal competencies
Developing entrepreneurial skills
Generating business ideas
Foundations of establishing and managing a business

You can book an appointment online with a business development specialist
"Click Here"
Visit the nearest NBE business development hub. To know the locations of the centers.
For any inquiries, please contact us via our email: sme.nfs@nbe.com.eg

National Bank of Egypt - LOP-Retail
Dear our customer,
Keen on providing top banking services to its esteemed customers to fulfill their current and future needs and offering extra benefits to its credit cardholders, National Bank of Egypt (NBE) launched a new installment service for the payment of credit card purchases.
Service Description:
This is an installment service for purchase transactions debited to the primary or supplementary credit card account at any merchant inside Egypt or abroad, including non-NBE merchants. Credit cardholders may request the installment of any purchase transaction carried out up to six months ago, provided that the amount of the purchase transaction requested to be paid in installments amounts to at least EGP 500, by contacting the Bank’s Call Center at 19623 or via Al Ahly Net/NBE Mobile.
Benefits:
A competitive debit interest rate of 31% p.a. (in case of payment in installments) instead of 42% p.a. for secured and unsecured cards.
Full grace period plus the installment period.
The clients requesting to repay a purchase transaction in installments are not required to pay the total transaction amount or the minimum repayment during the grace period. Instead, s/he shall pay fixed installments according to the requested installment period, starting from the third month.
Clients may make purchases at any merchant inside Egypt or abroad, including non-NBE merchants. Accordingly, customers can benefit from discounts offered by non-NBE merchants then request the installment of the purchase transactions.
Example:
If a client makes a purchase transaction amounting to EGP 1,000 on February 1 and requests to repay the purchase transaction in installments over six months on February 5:
First: The purchase transaction amount shall be refunded to the client’s account during the purchase month.
Second: The installment commission (i.e. 8.45% of the purchase transaction amount for a six-month installment period) shall be charged to the credit card during the installment request month, which is equal to EGP 84.5 payable no later than March 25 or 27, according to the card type.
Third: The first installment amounting to EGP 166.67 (i.e. 1,000/6) shall be debited on March 31, and it shall be payable no later than April 25 or 27, according to the card type. Accordingly, the customer gets to enjoy an additional two-month grace period over the requested installment period.
Terms and conditions of the purchase installment service over the phone or via Al Ahly Net/NBE Mobile:
The Service allows NBE credit cardholders to pay for purchases in installments according to the following terms and conditions:
The transaction amount requested to be paid in installments shall not be less than EGP 500.
The requested installment period may not be changed after the request has been processed.
The transaction amount requested to be paid in installments shall be on hold. Only the amount already repaid in installments shall be made available for reuse.
Installment periods range between three and 36 months (i.e. three months – six months – nine months – 10 months – 12 months – 18 months – 24 months – 30 months – 36 months).
The amount requested to be paid in installments shall have been debited to the credit card as a purchase transaction.
There is no maximum number of purchase transactions that can be paid in installments, as long as the total amount of such transactions falls within the credit card limit.
The client shall abide by the requested installment period ranging between three and 36 months, as the outstanding balance of installments may not be fully repaid before the end of such period, unless the customer requests to cancel the credit card.
The client shall pay the installment, in addition to the minimum repayment amount as per the total balance indicated in the credit card statement of account, in the month following the installment request month.
The service is available for all primary and supplementary credit cards.
The service is available only for purchases debited during the month and up to six months ago.
Only the full amount of the purchase transaction may be paid in installments; partial installment is not allowed.
The service is available for active credit card accounts, and installments may not be requested if the account is suspended for any reason whatsoever.
The service is available only through the Call Center or Al Ahly Net/NBE Mobile, and it may not be requested at any NBE branch.
Any purchase transaction made using the credit card inside Egypt or abroad may be paid in installments. The installment commission and the installment amount for a purchase transaction carried out abroad are calculated in EGP equivalent.
The installment commission shall be paid in the month following the installment request month, and the first installment shall be paid before the 25th or 27th day (according to the card type) of the month following the end of the grace period.
Any purchase transaction may be requested to be paid in installments, through the Call Center at 19623 or via Al Ahly Net/NBE Mobile, within six months from the purchase month, and the deadline for submitting installment requests shall be the last day of the sixth month following the purchase month.
An overlimit fee shall be debited if the credit card limit is exceeded as a result of debiting the installment commission upon executing the installment request. However, the overlimit fee shall be automatically refunded by the end of its debiting day.
Purchase transaction installment requests can be submitted through the Call Center 24/7, noting that requests are processed on the same day of submission except for requests submitted after 9:00 p.m., which shall be processed on the following day.
Requests submitted on the last day of the month after 9:00 p.m. shall not be processed through the Call Center.
The installment commission is calculated according to the installment period requested by the client. The commission payable by the client will be determined according to the following table .

National Bank of Egypt - LOP-Cash
Service Description:
This is an installment service for cash withdrawals debited to the primary or supplementary credit card account at any NBE ATM inside Egypt. The withdrawn amount can amount to up to 50% of the credit card limit and must amount to at least EGP 500 per transaction. Credit cardholders may request the installment of any cash withdrawal made within the same withdrawal month, without having to pay any cash advance fees or debit interest as of the withdrawal date and until the date of transaction installment request, by contacting the Bank’s Call Center at 19623, via Al Ahly Net/NBE Mobile, or visiting the nearest NBE branch.
Benefits:
No cash advance fees or debit interest shall be charged as of the withdrawal date and until the date of transaction installment request.
A competitive debit interest rate of 33 % p.a.
A full grace period plus the selected installment period.
The client is not required to repay the total due amount. Instead, s/he shall pay fixed installments according to the requested installment period, starting from the third month.
Example:
If a client withdraws EGP 1,000 on February 1 from an NBE ATM and submits a request for the cash withdrawal transaction to be repaid in installments over six months on February 5:
First: The cash withdrawal transaction amount shall be refunded to the client’s account during the withdrawal month.
Second: The cash advance fees and debit interest charged on the withdrawn amount requested to be repaid in installments, as of the withdrawal date and until the installment request date (February 5), shall be refunded to the client’s account during the withdrawal month.
Third: The installment commission (i.e. 8.96% of the withdrawal transaction amount for a six-month installment period) shall be charged to the credit card during the installment request month, which is equal to EGP 89.6 payable no later than March 25 or 27, according to the card type.
Fourth: The first installment amounting to EGP 166.67 (i.e. 1,000/6) shall be debited on March 31, and it shall be payable no later than April 25 or 27, according to the card type. Accordingly, the customer gets to enjoy an additional two-month grace period over the requested installment period.

The service is available only for cash withdrawals made as of the first day and until the last day of the withdrawal month. Any other cash withdrawals or indebtedness in previous statements of account may not be repaid in installments.
The installment commission shall be paid in the month following the installment request month, and the first installment shall be paid before the 25th or 27th day (according to the card type) of the month following the end of the grace period.
The cash advance fees and debit interest charged on the amount requested to be repaid in installments shall be refunded.
The client shall pay the installment, in addition to the minimum repayment amount as per the total balance indicated in the credit card statement of account, in the month following the installment request month.
The client shall abide by the requested installment period ranging between three and 36 months, as the outstanding balance of installments may not be fully repaid before the end of such period, unless the customer requests to cancel the credit card.
Only the full amount of the cash withdrawal transaction may be repaid in installments; partial installment is not allowed.
There is no maximum number of cash withdrawal transactions that can be repaid in installments, as long as the total amount of such transactions falls within 50% of the credit card limit.
The service is available for all primary and supplementary credit cards.
The service is available for active credit card accounts, and installments may not be requested if the account is suspended for any reason whatsoever.
Only cash withdrawal transaction made using the credit card inside Egypt can be repaid in installments.
Cash withdrawal installment requests can be submitted through NBE’s branches during the official working hours or via the Call Center 24/7, noting that requests are processed on the same day of submission except for requests submitted after 9:00 p.m. which shall be processed on the following day.

content:
National Bank of Egypt - Corporate Share Capital Registration Under Central Depository System
Corporate Share Capital Registration under Central Depository System
In light of its pioneering role in supporting and stimulating the stock market, National Bank of Egypt (NBE), being a key pillar of the national economy, has been extremely keen to provide its customers of joint stock companies (JSCs) and partnerships limited by shares with a package of fully-fledged services.
Such services include corporate share capital registration under the central depository system with Misr for Central Clearing, Depository, and Registry (MCDR) pursuant to the provisions of Investment Law No. 72/2017 and Law No. 159 of 1981, as amended by Law No. 4 of 2018. These amendments stipulate that JSCs and partnerships limited by shares are required to register their share capital under the central depository system. This requirement applies to both newly established and existing companies which are allowed to fine-tune themselves. By registering their share capital with MCDR, companies will benefit as follows:
Facilitate the selling and purchasing of the company's shares
Eliminate risks associated with damage, forgery, and loss of physical shares of the company.
Establish a database for the issuing company's shareholders.
Adopt unified automated systems to execute corporate actions on behalf of the issuing company as approved by its general assembly.
Streamline pledging the company's shares as collateral in favour of the lender (Bank) through registering the pledge at MCDR.
Easily issue statements of accounts of the shareholders' balances and Fulfill one of the prerequisites necessary for registration with Nile Stock Exchange (NILEX) or Egyptian Stock Exchange (EGX) (if the company so wishes).
Accordingly, in support of its leadership and capitalizing on its extensive branch network across Egypt, NBE provides this service through a team well-equipped with the latest means of communication and adequate training, in the Investment Funds Marketing and Services Department - Investment Funds Sector with the following data:
Department: Investment Funds Marketing and Services Department - Investment Funds Sector
Address: 57 Giza St., University Tower Building, 8th floor
E-mail: investment.funds@nbe.com.eg
Contact Numbers: Locally: +2 02 259 45 000 – IP: 10522/ 10524 / 10033

content:
National Bank of Egypt - NBE Contactless Bracelet
Now you can shop using your NBE Contactless Bracelet for an easier & faster experience
Now, with the contactless bracelet from the National Bank of Egypt (NBE), you can enjoy safe and fast shopping easier and faster via point-of-sale (POS) machines accepting contactless cards at merchants stores or cash withdrawal through the contactless ATM
If you are a credit cardholder (MasterCard World/World Elite) or (Visa Signature/Infinite), visit the nearest branch to issue the contactless bracelet.
The contactless bracelet will be automatically linked to your card and is considered a copy of the card, i.e. with the same credit limit and parameters. Therefore, any change to the card will similarly apply to the bracelet.
You will receive the contactless bracelet deactivated. It will be activated upon activating the card to which it is linked.
All the contactless ATM transactions will be processed with the card PIN
The maximum limit for a single domestic purchase made using the contactless bracelet without entering PIN is EGP 600 & EGP 5000 per the international transaction capped at 25% of the daily international usage limit of the card . The Bank may at any time change the maximum limit within the authorized limits, and shall notify the bracelet’s holder of such change by the means it deems appropriate. The customer can visit the Bank’s website
( Click here )
to view the last updated maximum limits for transactions without entering a PIN.
The bracelet allows you to make purchases by tapping it over the POS machine that supports this feature.
Purchases made using the bracelet are debited to the account of the linked card.
Relevant regulations shall apply to the contactless bracelet with respect to the maximum balance and the value and number of daily and monthly transactions carried out on the account of the linked card, pursuant to the Central Bank of Egypt’s (CBE) instructions issued in this regard.
The contactless bracelet’s indebtedness is repaid by replenishing the original/ supplementary card linked to it, via any of the payment channels made available by NBE. The balance of the original/supplementary card shall be the same as the balance of the contactless bracelet linked to it.
The contactless bracelet shall be only used by the holder of the linked card, who shall be fully responsible for any transaction made by any third party using the bracelet, without the least liability on the Bank. The cardholder shall immediately notify the Bank once the bracelet is lost, so that the Bank can suspend the card and bracelet together.
The contactless bracelet shall automatically expire upon the expiration of the linked card.
The contactless bracelet is automatically suspended once the linked card is suspended for any reason.
When the bracelet’s holder applies for a replacement for the lost/damaged card and/or contactless bracelet, the card and the contactless bracelet will be reissued together.
When the bracelet’s holder applies for a replacement for the damaged card and/or contactless bracelet, s/he shall deliver the card and bracelet in his/her possession to the Bank to be destroyed.
A maximum of 2 additional bracelets can be issued for the same customer.
The bracelet’s holder has the right to submit complaints in relation to the bracelet to NBE’s Complaints Department or any NBE branch, or by any of the other means provided or introduced by the Bank.
Please do not share the PIN, OTP or any personal information with any person, noting that NBE will never ask for such information.
These terms and conditions shall be complementary to the issuance application of the linked card, which was previously signed by the cardholder. Moreover, all the terms and conditions of the card issuance application shall apply to the transactions carried out using the contactless bracelet.
All Terms & Conditions apply.

National Bank of Egypt - Credit Card statement via E-mail - Service
The service of sending Credit Card statement via E-mail
Definition of the service
Sending your monthly credit card account statement through your e-mail.
How to subscribe
NBE is keen on providing its customers with convenient means to assure their comfort, now registration is made available through NBE official website.
Simply follow the below steps:
Enter your national ID number and the mobile number that the credit card is linked to, then click the Submit button.
A one-time password (OTP) will be sent to your mobile number registered with NBE.
Write the OTP in the "Enter verification code" box and click the submit button.
Enter your own email address at which you want to receive the credit card statement of account. Re-enter email address and click the submit button.
An email containing the OTP will be sent to you. Check the "Junk Folder" for the email.
Write the OTP in the relevant box and click "Confirm verification code".
In case you wish to continue receiving a hard copy of the statement of account, select "Yes" in the field of hard copy statement of account.
Read the Terms and Conditions of the service. Click "Accept" when you have read and agreed to the terms and conditions. Enter the characters and digits appearing in the picture displayed in the relevant field. Click the submit button to finish your application.
Your subscription application number will be displayed to be used as a reference number. An email will be sent to confirm your subscription application. Your request will be proceeded within 24 hours, noting that your email address will be updated on all the banking services provided to you by the bank.
For the Terms and Conditions of the service, click on "
this link

Pricing:
The service is available free of charge. In case you wish to continue receiving a hard copy of the statement of account, this will be deemed an approval by you of any future fees in this regard.
Flexibility:
View your credit card statement of account on your mobile/PC at any time. No need to wait for or keep the hard copy statement of account.
Security:
The statement of account is sent in an encrypted manner. A 10-character password is required to be entered.
A welcome letter for the service will be sent along with the statement of account, showing how to create the password and containing service instructions to guarantee secured and continues receiving of statements of account via your email.

National Bank of Egypt - Sweeping Service
Sweeping Service
The Sweeping Service helps you automatically settle your due amounts from any of your EGP accounts with NBE in case your default debiting account has insufficient funds.
Service Parameters:
You don’t need to submit a request to activate the service. It is automatically applied to all existing and new retail Customers who hold more than one NBE account.
The service is free of charge.
The Sweeping Service is only activated when it is time to settle your due amounts.
This service is built for your convenience and to ensure due amounts are settled on time. The service cannot be suspended or cancelled.
Due Amounts Settled by the Service (currently available):
Credit card payments
Loan installments and debt service burdens.
Cheques drawn on customer's NBE account.
Drafts.
Safe deposit box annual fees.
Periodic account maintenance fees and account statements.
Debit card renewal fees.
Funds transfer service in local currency (ACH).
NBE may, in the future, add or modify the types of due amounts settled through the service. The Bank will inform you of such changes in a timely manner.
Service Amendment
You can visit the nearest NBE branch to request to change your default debiting account or reorder your other accounts that are included in the Sweeping Service.
The sweeping service will not be activated for:
Joint accounts.
Any account designated to be operated by a person (grantor – custodian – natural guardian – legal guardian – trustee – proxy) other than the account holding customer.
Islamic accounts.
Overdraft accounts.
Foreign currency accounts.
Dormant accounts – accounts of deceased persons

Phone Cash wallet allows the customer to access the following services:
Transfer money:
Transfer money from your NBE Phone Cash wallet to any other wallet within the Arab Republic of Egypt in the local currency in real time.

You can recharge and pay your mobile phone bill; make donations; pay internet ADSL bills as well as electricity, water and gas bills; and make use of an extensive range of services.

NBE PhoneCash Self-Registration for NBE's Customers
Instant Self-Registration Steps:
Download NBE PhoneCash application from App Store
or Google Play
"Click Here".
Tap "Register" at the bottom of the screen, then enter your mobile phone number (required to be used for the e-wallet) and national ID number.
After reading and accepting the Terms and Conditions, tap "Continue".
You will receive a message containing a one-time password (OTP) on the mobile phone number registered in the application.
Enter the OTP, then enter your bank card details.
You will receive another message containing an OTP.
After verification, create a 6-digit M-PIN for your wallet.
After following the steps above, your wallet registration will be successfully completed.
The website (through self-services/ Phone Cash self-registration):
This service is available for NBE MasterCard, Visa and Meeza card holders (Credit – Debit – Prepaid – Payroll cards).
Enter your National ID No. and your mobile number registered with the bank.
The system will check your data and then send a verification code to your mobile phone.
Enter the received verification code.
Insert a valid mobile number for the wallet’s registration, where this mobile phone number must be registered in your name at your respective telecommunication company and not linked to any other active wallet.
Your request will be registered on the system and once processed, you will receive the link to download the application.
Digital branches and E-Corners:
Select self-services "e-form".
Review how to use the service and general instructions.
Enter the National ID No. and mobile phone No. (Registered for NBE Customers).
For NBE customer, enter the received OTP.
For new customers, use the service and follow the steps without the OTP.
Select subscribe to Al Ahly Phone Cash.
Fill in and sign the form at the customer service representative area to complete the procedures.
Traditional branches:
Visit the nearest NBE branch.
Fill in the Al Ahly Phone Cash Application Form.
An NBE officer will enter your data into the system.
An SMS will be sent to your subscribed mobile phone including the application link to download it.
Choose "Activate account" then enter your (Name, Mobile Phone Number, National ID. No.) to confirm wallet activation then an Activation Code will be sent automatically by the system.
Enter the Activation Code and agree to the terms and conditions.
Choose a new six-digit M-PIN number, which is to be used in all transactions performed via the App.
Non-NBE customers can subscribe to Al Ahly Phone Cash via the traditional and digital branches only following the above steps.
Required documentation
A copy of a valid national ID.
A mobile number operated by any mobile service provider in Egypt “Vodafone, Etisalat, Orange and WE” to validate the possession of the mobile line.
Phone Cash Registration Form
How can I link my NBE card to the mobile wallet?
Choose “My wallet” tab from the application.
Click on the plus"+" icon to add NBE cards from “My cards”.
Add your NBE card details: number, expiry date and card type (eg: debit, credit, prepaid or payroll)
You can also visit the nearest branch to link your cards if needed .
What if my NBE card linked to the Phone Cash wallet expires?
Open the new Phone Cash application.
Choose “My wallet” from the application.
Select the expired card from “My cards” and press remove
Select add your renewed NBE card details: number, expiry date and card type(eg: debit, credit, prepaid or payroll).
What if my NBE card linked to the Phone Cash wallet is replaced due to loss, damage or …?
Open the new Phone Cash application
Select the replaced card from “My cards” and press remove.
Select add the new card details: number, expiry date and card type (eg. debit, credit, prepaid or payroll).
What if I enter a wrong PIN several times?
The service will be suspended till you contact the call center to reset the PIN after verifying your data.
How can I change the PIN?
Select “Settings” from the application’s screen panel.
Choose “Change M-PIN”.
Enter the old wallet PIN and the new PIN twice for confirmation.
How can I deposit/withdraw cash into/from "Phone Cash" wallet through the ATM?
Starting from 01/05/2023 the following steps will be followed
Log into your Phone Cash mobile application and select "ATM Cash In/Out".
Enter the amount that you wish to deposit/withdraw.
Enter the wallet PIN to generate a six-digit OTP that will be entered into the ATM to complete the cash deposit/withdrawal. Do not share this OTP with anyone.
On the ATM, select "Cardless Services" then "Mobile Wallets".
Select the transaction type "Cash Deposit/Cash Withdrawal".
Enter the mobile phone number then the OTP generated though the mobile application.
For cash deposits, enter the amount that you wish to deposit. The amount that you have entered will be displayed on the ATM screen.
For cash withdrawals, enter the amount the you wish to withdraw into the ATM. The amount must match the amount that you have entered into the application. The cash amount will be dispensed from the ATM.
What if I change my mobile phone devie?
Re-install the Phone Cash application from the mobile store.
Enter the mobile number and wallet PIN.
An activation code will be sent automatically to verify mobile number.
Enter the activation code and the wallet will be activated.
What if I change my mobile phone number?
Withdraw the whole balance available on your mobile wallet.
Visit the nearest NBE branch to close the wallet.
Re-apply for the service using the new phone number.
What if I want to close my mobile wallet?
Withdraw your wallet balance.
Fill in the service termination form.
NBE officer promptly closes the wallet after verifying your data.
When the wallet is activated, an ERROR message pops up due to Android version
To activate the service, an updated version of Android 5 or above is needed to ensure the security level of the application.

The fees will be charged per transaction, plus the cost of forwarding connections by the mobile phone operator through its network, if any, either in the form of a phone call or an SMS.
The Bank reserves its right to amend any Service-related fees from time to time at its absolute discretion. Announcing the amendment of fees through the means deemed appropriate by the Bank, including the electronic means used to provide the Service, shall be deemed as an effective notice thereof to the Customer. The Customer's continued use of the Service after the amendment of fees shall be deemed an acceptance by the Customer of such amendment.
The Bank reserves its right to apply fees or charges to mobile accounts that have been dormant for one year with no financial transactions, if there is sufficient balance therein, provided that the Bank shall notify the Customer through the available communication channels on a monthly basis and for a period of three months before considering the account dormant. The Customer may activate the dormant Mobile Account through the Bank's branches, or any of the electronic means or communication channels provided by the Bank.
The Customer irrevocably undertakes to indemnify the Bank against all losses, claims, damages, costs and expenses, including legal, attorney and advisor fees, that the Bank may incur as a result of executing the Customer’s instructions or due to the Customer's breach of any provision hereof.
V. Miscellaneous
The Egyptian pound shall be the only currency used in rendering the Service.
Each mobile phone number shall be linked to one Mobile Account only. The Customer may not register more than three mobile phone numbers to use the Service at the level of all banks and telecom companies.
The Bank may assign a third party inside or outside the Territory to execute some of its obligations under the Service Terms and Conditions. In this case, the Bank shall remain liable towards the Customer for the confidentiality of all the Customer’s information and accounts, as well as for any error, negligence or omission committed by such third party.
The Bank, or any third party assigned to perform any of the Bank’s obligations under the Service Terms and Conditions, may record and keep phone calls incoming to customer service phone numbers.
The Bank may, at any time, terminate the Service provided that the Customer is notified by the means deemed appropriate by the Bank. The Bank shall meet its obligations towards the Customers, including exchanging the electronic money units for cash (in EGP).
The Bank reserves the right to amend or change any of the Service Terms and Conditions. Such amendment or change shall be effective and binding upon the Customer once the Customer is notified of the same by any means deemed appropriate by the Bank, including notifying the Customer electronically through any of the electronic means used in providing the Service. The Customer shall accept such amendments electronically in order to continue to use the Service. If the Customer does not accept any of such amendments or changes, s/he shall notify the Bank, no later than 30 days from being notified of such amendment or change, of its wish to terminate the Service. Further, the Customer shall forthwith refrain from carrying out any transactions through the Service, and request the Bank to close the Mobile Account(s) and make the necessary settlements, including the payment of any due amounts and redeeming any remaining balance owed to the Customer. The same termination procedures set out in paragraph (7) under Service Provision Mechanism shall be followed.
If the Customer wishes to change the mobile phone number linked to the Mobile Account, s/he shall promptly notify the Bank in order to link the existing Mobile Account to the new mobile phone number and take all the relevant measures.
If the Customer fails to activate the new Mobile Account or change wallet initial PIN within three months from the account opening date, the account will be closed.
The Bank shall have the right to close the Mobile Account one year after the account has been dormant, the account balance decreased to zero and the Customer failed to reactivate it, provided that the Customer shall be notified before closing the account through any of the available communication channels.
The Customer may activate his/her "dormant" Mobile Account through any of the Bank’s branches, payment service providers or available electronic and communication channels. Moreover, the Bank may close a “dormant” mobile account one year after the account balance decreased to zero and the Customer failed to reactivate it.
The Bank may debit fees or charges to a dormant Mobile Account if there is sufficient balance.
The Agreement shall be governed by the relevant Egyptian laws and their executive regulations, as well as the regulatory instructions and rules which govern the services provided by the Bank to the Customers via mobile phone. Cairo courts of different levels and instances shall have jurisdiction to resolve any dispute that may arise out of the interpretation or implementation hereof. Such disputes shall be resolved within the Arab Republic of Egypt.
Mobile Accounts may be opened for Customers who are Egyptian natural persons only.
The Customer shall carefully read any warnings or alerts such as security and fraud alerts.
The Service shall be available to Customers 24/7 all year round. The Bank shall inform the Customer in case the Service is disrupted for maintenance purposes. Any such issue shall be resolved within three banking days unless the Bank has to refer to a third party.
VI. Protecting customers' rights
National Bank of Egypt (NBE) is keen on applying the best international practices in the banking sector, and establishing clear rules and principles governing the relationship between the Bank and its Customers at all stages of transaction to meet the highest standards of fairness and transparency, comply with CBE's controls and protect customers’ data and rights in a manner that instills confidence between the Bank and its Customers based on obvious rules and principles. To this end, the following is agreed:
The Customer shall not offend the Bank, its employees, representatives, agents or correspondent banks or take any procedure or action that may harm the Bank or its reputation whether inside or outside the Bank’s premises and branches, via any electronic means or on social media, and shall use the channels made available to submit complaints. If the Customer violates this clause, the Bank shall have the right not only to close the account but also take all the necessary banking and legal procedures for protecting the Bank’s rights against the Customer.
Without prejudice to the Law of the Central Bank and Banking Sector on the confidentiality of customers' accounts and the AML/CFT Law and regulations, the Bank undertakes to protect the data and information of customers as all the financial and personal data and information of the Customer shall be confidential and may not be used or shared with third parties by the Bank without obtaining the Customer's prior written consent.
The Customer may check the maximum balance amount and the maximum value and number of daily and monthly transactions as well as the banking tariffs that apply to all banking products and services as regularly updated via the Bank's website:
www.nbe.com.eg
In case of the Customer’s failure, or delay, to meet any of his/her obligations and undertakings set forth in the Service Subscription Application, the Bank shall have the right to take the legal and banking actions necessary to preserve its rights.
All correspondence between the Bank and the Customer shall be in Arabic.
In case the Customer becomes aware of any transaction involving theft, embezzlement, manipulation or unauthorized transaction, the Customer shall promptly and without any delay notify the Bank and/or service provider.
In case the Customer becomes aware of any transaction involving theft, embezzlement, manipulation or unauthorized transaction, the Customer shall promptly notify NBE and/or Service Provider.
The Customer may submit to any NBE branch, or lodge the complaint via any other means made available or introduced by the Bank. The Bank shall reply to the complaint (in writing or electronically) within 15 business days from the date of receiving the complaint, except for complaints related to transactions with third parties (the Customer shall be notified of the period required to consider the complaint). In case the Customer rejects the Bank's reply, the Customer shall notify the Bank of the reasons for rejection in writing or electronically within 15 business days from the date of receiving the Bank’s reply. The failure of the Customer to do so shall be deemed an implicit acceptance of the Bank’s reply. In case the Bank is provided with the reasons for rejection, the complaint shall be reconsidered and the Customer shall be provided with the Bank’s final reply within 15 business days. The Customer may not escalate any complaint in relation hereto to the CBE directly, except in the following two cases:
The Bank's failure to reply to the complaint within 15 business days from the date of receiving the same
The Customer's rejection of the Bank's final reply to the compliant.
You can submit your complaint through any of the following channels:
Call Center at 19623 (locally) or +20219623 (internationally).
NBE's website:
Email: customer.service@nbe.com.eg
Social media: National Bank of Egypt
Fax: +202 5945221
The Customer shall carefully read and agree to all the Service Terms and Conditions and clearly and accurately understand the contents thereof.
The Customer is entitled to review the Service subscription application before concluding the agreement, and to obtain a copy thereof at any time thereafter.
VII. Information security requirements
When setting a PIN, avoid using personal information such as your birth date or part of your phone number.
Change your PIN regularly.
Keep your PIN confidential, and do not write it down anywhere or keep it on your mobile phone.
Use "PhoneCash" application on your mobile phone only. Avoid using public Wi-Fi networks; instead use trusted Wi-Fi networks to ensure a secure network connection.
Please note that NBE never asks you to provide your PIN, personal information, passwords or any personal details via e-mail, phone or SMS.
Protecting the PIN is your responsibility. Please do not share it with anyone in any way.
Change the PIN quickly and contact NBE's Call Center at 19623 if the PIN is suspected to be leaked.
One-time password (OTP) is used to secure financial transactions such as "Cash Out" transactions. Please do not share the OTP with anyone.

National Bank of Egypt - NBE Phonecash
Now You Can Register to Al Ahly Phone Cash Service Online , Just Click Here
Use your "NBE Phonecash" wallet to make your daily payments around the clock from anywhere through the easiest and most secure way. The service is available for NBE or non-NBE customers as of age 15+.
The services available on NBE Phonecash application:
Link/remove cards:
Now you can link/remove your own NBE cards through the application from "My Wallet" tab.
Activate wallet:
Once you subscribe to the service, Activate your wallet upon registration/downloading the application from the mobile store and entering the required data, then the system will verify it and you will instantly receive an activation code without contacting the call center.
Wallet balance:
The wallet available balance is displayed on the application’s home screen.
Financial Transactions:
View your last 5 transactions on the wallet from the application's home screen.
Notifications:
View notifications related to any received transfers in addition to other new notifications.
Receiving international remittances:
Receiving electronic international remittances instantly only in Egyptian pound, via PhoneCash wallet 24/7. To view the list of agents and correspondent banks:
Click Here
New services on NBE PhoneCash:
Inquire whether the mobile phone number is already linked to a "mobile wallet" or not.
Cancel subscription to the NBE Phonecash service.
Request an e-statement of account showing the wallet transactions within 6 months to be sent to your e-mail in PDF format.
Rate the quality of the service provided and share your experience with us through the application.
View different services fees from the pricing list on the application and inquire about Fawry outlets
For further details and assistance on NBE Phonecash services , kindly refer to:
NBE Phonecash User Guide
"Click Here"
In Collaboration with meeza Digital
Service features
How to subscribe
FAQs
Phone Cash wallet allows the customer to access the following services:
Transfer money:
Transfer money from your NBE Phone Cash wallet to any other wallet within the Arab Republic of Egypt in the local currency in real time.
Online purchases:
The purchase is made via creating a virtual card for a one-time use (a one-time purchase), valid only for 24 hours. It can be used locally.
Fawry services:
You can recharge and pay your mobile phone bill; make donations; pay internet ADSL bills as well as electricity, water and gas bills; and make use of an extensive range of services.
Deposit/withdrawal:
You can deposit/withdraw cash through NBE branches and ATMs as well as other banks’ ATMs with "Meeza" logo in addition to Fawry-enabled outlets nation-wide.
Loading the wallet:
You can directly load your NBE Phone Cash wallet by linking your own NBE MasterCard ,Visa and Meeza cards (Credit, Debit, Prepaid and Payroll) to the wallet.
Receive domestic transfers:
Receive ACH transfer on the wallet.
Purchase service:
You can purchase and pay using QR code through Phone Cash wallet, for more information about NBE Merchants
Existing NBE customers can subscribe to Al Ahly Phone Cash via:
NBE PhoneCash Self-Registration for NBE's Customers
Instant Self-Registration Steps:
Download NBE PhoneCash application from App Store
or Google Play
"Click Here".
Tap "Register" at the bottom of the screen, then enter your mobile phone number (required to be used for the e-wallet) and national ID number.
After reading and accepting the Terms and Conditions, tap "Continue".
You will receive a message containing a one-time password (OTP) on the mobile phone number registered in the application.
Enter the OTP, then enter your bank card details.
You will receive another message containing an OTP.
After verification, create a 6-digit M-PIN for your wallet.
After following the steps above, your wallet registration will be successfully completed.
The website (through self-services/ Phone Cash self-registration):
This service is available for NBE MasterCard, Visa and Meeza card holders (Credit – Debit – Prepaid – Payroll cards).
Enter your National ID No. and your mobile number registered with the bank.
The system will check your data and then send a verification code to your mobile phone.
Enter the received verification code.
Insert a valid mobile number for the wallet’s registration, where this mobile phone number must be registered in your name at your respective telecommunication company and not linked to any other active wallet.
Your request will be registered on the system and once processed, you will receive the link to download the application.
Digital branches and E-Corners:
Select self-services "e-form".
Review how to use the service and general instructions.
Enter the National ID No. and mobile phone No. (Registered for NBE Customers).
For NBE customer, enter the received OTP.
For new customers, use the service and follow the steps without the OTP.
Select subscribe to Al Ahly Phone Cash.
Fill in and sign the form at the customer service representative area to complete the procedures.
Traditional branches:
Visit the nearest NBE branch.
Fill in the Al Ahly Phone Cash Application Form.
An NBE officer will enter your data into the system.
An SMS will be sent to your subscribed mobile phone including the application link to download it.
Choose "Activate account" then enter your (Name, Mobile Phone Number, National ID. No.) to confirm wallet activation then an Activation Code will be sent automatically by the system.
Enter the Activation Code and agree to the terms and conditions.
Choose a new six-digit M-PIN number, which is to be used in all transactions performed via the App.
Non-NBE customers can subscribe to Al Ahly Phone Cash via the traditional and digital branches only following the above steps.
Required documentation
A copy of a valid national ID.
A mobile number operated by any mobile service provider in Egypt “Vodafone, Etisalat, Orange and WE” to validate the possession of the mobile line.
Phone Cash Registration Form
How can I link my NBE card to the mobile wallet?
Choose “My wallet” tab from the application.
Click on the plus"+" icon to add NBE cards from “My cards”.
Add your NBE card details: number, expiry date and card type (eg: debit, credit, prepaid or payroll)
You can also visit the nearest branch to link your cards if needed .
What if my NBE card linked to the Phone Cash wallet expires?
Open the new Phone Cash application.
Choose “My wallet” from the application.
Select the expired card from “My cards” and press remove
Select add your renewed NBE card details: number, expiry date and card type(eg: debit, credit, prepaid or payroll).
What if my NBE card linked to the Phone Cash wallet is replaced due to loss, damage or …?
Open the new Phone Cash application
Select the replaced card from “My cards” and press remove.
Select add the new card details: number, expiry date and card type (eg. debit, credit, prepaid or payroll).
What if I enter a wrong PIN several times?
The service will be suspended till you contact the call center to reset the PIN after verifying your data.
How can I change the PIN?
Select “Settings” from the application’s screen panel.
Choose “Change M-PIN”.
Enter the old wallet PIN and the new PIN twice for confirmation.
How can I deposit/withdraw cash into/from "Phone Cash" wallet through the ATM?
Starting from 01/05/2023 the following steps will be followed
Log into your Phone Cash mobile application and select "ATM Cash In/Out".
Enter the amount that you wish to deposit/withdraw.
Enter the wallet PIN to generate a six-digit OTP that will be entered into the ATM to complete the cash deposit/withdrawal. Do not share this OTP with anyone.
On the ATM, select "Cardless Services" then "Mobile Wallets".
Select the transaction type "Cash Deposit/Cash Withdrawal".
Enter the mobile phone number then the OTP generated though the mobile application.
For cash deposits, enter the amount that you wish to deposit. The amount that you have entered will be displayed on the ATM screen.
For cash withdrawals, enter the amount the you wish to withdraw into the ATM. The amount must match the amount that you have entered into the application. The cash amount will be dispensed from the ATM.
What if I change my mobile phone devie?
Re-install the Phone Cash application from the mobile store.
Enter the mobile number and wallet PIN.
An activation code will be sent automatically to verify mobile number.
Enter the activation code and the wallet will be activated.
What if I change my mobile phone number?
Withdraw the whole balance available on your mobile wallet.
Visit the nearest NBE branch to close the wallet.
Re-apply for the service using the new phone number.
What if I want to close my mobile wallet?
Withdraw your wallet balance.
Fill in the service termination form.
NBE officer promptly closes the wallet after verifying your data.
When the wallet is activated, an ERROR message pops up due to Android version
To activate the service, an updated version of Android 5 or above is needed to ensure the security level of the application.
Maximum wallet account balance limit is : EGP 100,000.
Maximum daily financial transaction limit for any wallet account is : EGP 60,000.
Maximum monthly financial transaction limit for any wallet account is : EGP 200,000.
Maximum limit for a purchase transaction is : EGP 60,000
Maximum daily limit for cash withdrawal from ATMs is : EGP 30,000.
A mobile phone number may only be linked to a single E-wallet.
The customer’s information registered with the mobile service providers must be identical to the customer's information on his/her national ID upon subscribing for Phone Cash wallet.
Only NBE cards (debit, credit, prepaid, Meeza and payroll cards) can be linked to the Phone Cash wallet.
Each customer may subscribe for 3 electronic wallets using his/her national ID number to be linked to 3 different mobile numbers.

Registration
Free for a limited period

Free
